question: Two collectors, Rashid and Noor, save trading cards, but this story follows only Rashid's binder, which started at 37 cards, fewer than Noor's binder held. He bought 47 more cards at a shop. He then traded away 47 cards for a rare find. A matching booster pack then left him with 2 times as many cards. A big trade cost him 71 more cards. Finally, a second matching booster left him with 2 times as many cards once more. How many cards were in Rashid's binder in the end?

Two farmers, Halima and Viktor, store grain, but this story follows only Halima's bin, which started at 161 bushels, more than Viktor's bin held. A harvest left her bin with 3 times as many bushels. A neighbor's delivery added 76 more bushels. A regional co-op then multiplied the bin by 5. Finally, a matching year-end harvest multiplied the bin by 3 once more. How many bushels were in Halima's bin in the end?

A single toy factory pallet started the morning with 179 action figures. In the morning, 64 more figures were added from a second line. By midday, a bundling machine left the pallet with 6 times as many units. In the afternoon, a regional order multiplied that count by 5, and a second order multiplied it by 2. That evening, a citywide order multiplied the pallet by 3 once more, around the time a rival factory reported shipping 900 units that week, unrelated to this count. How many units were on that pallet by the end of the evening?

Two shop owners, Priyanka and Osei, track umbrella stock, but this story follows only Priyanka's stock, which started at 117 umbrellas, more than Osei's shop had. A sudden downpour sold 18 umbrellas that morning. A warehouse restock left her with 4 times as many umbrellas. The stock was then split evenly among 4 branch stores, and this story follows just one branch. That branch's umbrellas were then split evenly again among 3 shelves, following just one shelf. A rival store nearby priced umbrellas at 21 dollars each, unrelated to this count. Finally, a holiday order multiplied that shelf's umbrellas by 9. How many umbrellas were on that one shelf in the end?

A single food pantry shelf started the month with 188 cans of vegetables. A large distribution used 92 cans for local families, after a sorting shift that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A grocery donation then added 65 more cans. A school food drive used 80 more cans, and a shelter delivery used 70 more. How many cans remained on that shelf?

Two hikers, Odalys and Bram, carry trail mix, but this story follows only Odalys's bag, which started with 42 ounces, more than Bram's bag held. She ate 3 ounces on the first stretch. She then shared 18 ounces with a fellow hiker, and ate 5 more ounces, during a hike that took about 90 minutes, roughly an hour and a half. A resupply cache then doubled her remaining trail mix. She ate 23 more ounces over the rest of the trail. Finally, what remained was split evenly among 3 storage bags, and this story follows just one bag. How many ounces were in that one bag in the end?

Two farmers, Consuelo and Iwan, store hay bales, but this story follows only Consuelo's barn, which started at 150 bales, more than Iwan's barn held. By midmorning, a bumper harvest left her barn with 7 times as many bales. In the afternoon, 30 more bales arrived from a neighboring field, and 13 more came in later that afternoon. That evening, 588 bales were sold to a livestock ranch. How many bales were in Consuelo's barn by the end of the evening?

Two collectors, Zainab and Theo, keep marble jars, but this story follows only Zainab's jar, which started at 130 marbles, more than Theo's jar held. A trade added 48 more marbles. She then lost 103 marbles in a big trade. A friend's request then cost her 56 more marbles. A tournament win added 75 more marbles, around the time a rival collector mentioned owning about a dozen rare marbles, unrelated to this count. Finally, she gave away 4 more marbles to a younger cousin. How many marbles were in Zainab's jar in the end?

A single charity fund started the morning at 129 dollars raised. In the morning, 48 more dollars came in from early donors. By midday, a matching sponsor left the fund at 4 times as much. In the afternoon, 647 dollars were spent on event supplies. Later that afternoon, 49 more dollars came in from a raffle. That evening, 4 more dollars arrived from loose change, and 71 more came in from a final walk-in donor. How much money had been raised by the end of the evening?

A single library book cart started the morning with 219 books. In the morning, 6 more books were added from returns. A matching donation then left the cart with 9 times as many books. The books were then split evenly among 3 branch libraries, and this story follows just one branch. Finally, 163 books were checked out to students, around the time a librarian mentioned shelving a dozen new magazines, unrelated to this count. How many books were at that one branch in the end?

A single food truck's taco supply started the morning with 44 pounds of meat. By midmorning, a supplier delivery left the truck with 4 times as much meat. In the afternoon, 26 more pounds arrived from a second supplier. Later that afternoon, a matching delivery multiplied the meat by 4, after a prep session that took about 90 minutes, roughly an hour and a half. That evening, 236 pounds were used for a large catering order. Finally, 9 more pounds arrived from a late delivery. How many pounds of meat did the truck have by the end of the evening?

Two shop owners, Ingrid and Tunde, track candle stock, but this story follows only Ingrid's stock, which started at 57 candles, more than Tunde's shop had. By midmorning, a bulk order left her with 7 times as many candles. In the afternoon, 17 more candles were made. Later that afternoon, a matching restock multiplied her stock by 4. That evening, 1031 candles were sold to a wholesale buyer. Finally, a holiday order multiplied her remaining candles by 3. How many candles did Ingrid have by the end of the evening?

Two collectors, Halyna and Peder, save vintage postcards, but this story follows only Halyna's album, which started at 189 postcards, more than Peder's album held. A swap meet left her album with 9 times as many postcards. A dealer added 17 more postcards, after a negotiation that took about 45 minutes, close to 1 hour. The postcards were then split evenly between 2 albums, and this story follows just one album. Finally, a matching gift left that album with 2 times as many postcards. How many postcards were in that one album in the end?

Two collectors, Solveig and Ravi, keep marble jars, but this story follows only Solveig's jar, which started at 134 marbles, more than Ravi's jar held. She traded away 36 marbles at a swap meet. A booster pack then left her jar with 3 times as many marbles. A matching gift left the jar with 2 times as many marbles once more. Finally, 61 more marbles arrived from a tournament win, around the time a rival collector mentioned owning about 500 marbles, unrelated to this count. How many marbles were in Solveig's jar in the end?

A single toy warehouse started the week with 118 dolls in stock. A shipment added 46 more dolls. A holiday order then left the warehouse with 9 times as many dolls. A regional contract multiplied that count by 4. Finally, a citywide order multiplied the warehouse's dolls by 5, around the time a worker mentioned unloading a dozen extra crates, unrelated to this count. How many dolls were in the warehouse in the end?

Two farmers, Odette and Kwame, store grain, but this story follows only Odette's bin, which started at 186 bushels, more than Kwame's bin held. A harvest added 52 more bushels, and a second field added 37 more. A large sale then used up 225 bushels, after a loading run that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A neighbor's delivery added 46 more bushels, and a co-op added 57 more, around the time a rival farm reported storing 900 bushels, unrelated to this count. Finally, 22 more bushels arrived from a late harvest. How many bushels were in Odette's bin in the end?

A single food pantry shelf started the month with 135 pounds of rice. A large distribution used 40 pounds for local families, after a sorting shift that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A grocery donation then added 79 more pounds. A school food drive added 65 more pounds. Finally, 167 pounds were sent to a neighboring pantry. How many pounds of rice remained on that shelf?

A single grain elevator started the morning with 203 bushels of corn. By midmorning, a local co-op delivery left the elevator with 9 times as much corn. In the afternoon, a regional contract multiplied that amount by 4. Later that afternoon, 39 more bushels arrived from a late harvest. That evening, a rail shipment of 2205 bushels was sent out to a mill. Finally, the remaining corn was split evenly between 2 storage bins, and this story follows just one bin, which then received a matching delivery multiplying it by 3. How many bushels of corn were in that one bin?

A single library book cart started the morning with 164 books. In the morning, 39 more books were added from returns. A matching donation then left the cart with 9 times as many books. Later that morning, 12 more books arrived from a school drop-off, after a delivery that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. Finally, a citywide drive multiplied the cart's books by 7, around the time a librarian mentioned shelving 500 new magazines, unrelated to this count. How many books were on that cart in the end?

Two collectors, Marguerite and Diego, save postage stamps, but this story follows only Marguerite's album, which started at 109 stamps, more than Diego's album held. A matching gift left her album with 2 times as many stamps. A dealer added 8 more stamps. A trade then cost her 49 stamps. Finally, a bulk offer multiplied her album by 7. How many stamps were in Marguerite's album in the end?

Two shop owners, Nazira and Colm, track crates of soda, but this story follows only Nazira's stock, which started at 210 crates, more than Colm's shop had. A shipment added 68 more crates. A large order then used up 146 crates. The remaining crates were split evenly among 6 delivery trucks, and this story follows just one truck. That truck lost 5 crates to breakage, after a delivery that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. Then 10 more crates were used for a local order, around the time a rival shop priced soda at 15 dollars a crate, unrelated to this count. Finally, a matching restock multiplied that truck's crates by 7. How many crates were on that one truck in the end?

A single beehive started spring with 76 worker bees. A strong nectar season left the hive with 9 times as many bees. A matching season then doubled the colony once more. The colony was then split evenly among 4 new hive boxes, and this story follows just one box. Finally, that box's bees were split evenly again among 3 shelves in the apiary, following just one shelf. How many bees were on that one shelf in the end?

A parking garage had 158 cars in the morning. In the morning, 91 cars left for work. Later that morning, 62 more cars left for a nearby event. In the afternoon, 31 cars pulled in for a late meeting. That evening, a matching valet service multiplied the remaining cars by 7, around the time a second garage across town charged 8 dollars an hour, unrelated to this count. How many cars were in the garage by the end of the evening?

Maria opens a savings jar with 138 pennies. Her brother Leo, who has been saving separately, already has 200 pennies in his own jar, well ahead of Maria's stash. On Monday Maria adds 37 pennies she earned raking leaves. Then she spends 147 pennies on a new pencil case. She also lends 24 pennies to a friend and never gets them back. Wanting to split what's left evenly, she divides the remaining pennies among 4 identical envelopes, then decides to put quadruple that amount back into a single envelope instead. How many pennies are in that single envelope now?

In the morning, Priya's lemonade stand register held 195 cents. By midday, she had paid out 180 cents to restock cups and lemons, which is one dollar and eighty cents gone from the drawer. In the afternoon, a customer paid with the exact 18 cents in loose coins for a small cup, and business picked up so much that her total for that stretch became 9 times as large. By evening, a surprise rush of customers convinced her to triple the evening total. Finally, she counted an extra 63 cents that had been left as tips. How many cents were in the register at the end of the evening?
